ceiling_directive: Replace the explicit \(2^p\)-state construction with an on-demand compressed fragment automaton whose number of visited states is polynomial in \(p,m\) and the emitted tuples, thereby obtaining conventional output-polynomial total complexity on the same component-aligned frontier.
improvement_directive: Strengthen the component-aligned enumeration theorem by avoiding materialization of all removed subsets and prove a polynomial bound in \(p,m,N_{\mathrm{out}}^{\mathrm{CA}}\) for the compressed live-fragment graph. Carry the same improvement through the rational bit-complexity theorem.
critique: The published unrestricted-cross-view class is proved to admit every order and no common ancestry, so the pairing-informative result applies only to the note-defined component-aligned subclass with cross-coordinate orthogonality and positive-definite coordinate blocks. Within that subclass, the note proves q-path/fiber equivalence and exact-once tuple enumeration, but the algorithm still constructs an explicit \(2^p\) subset space even when the numerical output is a singleton. Thus the advertised output sensitivity is only a multiplicative refinement of a subset-exponential algorithm, not conventional output-polynomial enumeration or polynomial delay. The framing accurately states these limitations, but the combination of a specially constructed subclass and unavoidable exponential preprocessing keeps the delivered result below the field-tier target.
